clue.text: Playmaker Spanish rate for juggling and retaining ball

indicators.note: retaining means holding something within, so the ball goes inside the shuffled letters
juggling tosses things about, so the letters of Spanish rate are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A Spanish football playmaker juggles the ball while someone sets a rate for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playmaker' suggests a footballer, but here it means a writer of plays. 'for juggling' rearranges SPANISH RATE and 'retaining' puts O inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian comic dramatist wrote plays such as The Birds and The Frogs, so he was literally a maker of plays.

clue.text: Excuse to work out topless, holding up muscles

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece placed above another is holding it up

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles

indicators.note: topless means the top, here the first letter, is removed

parts.note: to work out a problem is to solve it

explanation.surface: Someone excuses themselves from a topless workout because their muscles are holding them up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'holding up' means sitting on top; 'topless' removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone in the sense of pardoning or freeing them from blame is to absolve them.

clue.text: He won't appreciate current grid

parts.note: something current is in, that is fashionable
a grate is a grid of metal bars, as in a fireplace

explanation.surface: A man who will not value the grid that supplies the electric current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like electricity beside 'grid', but it means fashionable, giving IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person is one who does not appreciate kindness shown to him.

clue.text: International politician, well positioned in case of flood, rides here?

indicators.note: being well positioned in something means sitting inside it, so the politician goes into the case

parts.note: Noah's vessel, the Ark, was the case that held the animals through the Flood
an MEP, Member of the European Parliament, is a politician working across nations

explanation.surface: An international politician on high ground during a flood, asking about rides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of flood' reads as an emergency, but it is Noah's vessel; 'well positioned in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement parks built around a theme are where people go for fairground rides, hence the question mark.

clue.text: More than one top dog's outspoken

indicators.note: outspoken signals that the word is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: dog's read as dogs, Pekes being Pekinese dogs

explanation.surface: A top dog is rather outspoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top dog' looks like a single phrase; 'top' belongs to the definition and 'dog's' is the word spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaks are summits, the tops of mountains, and the plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Pound fills a poem with it

indicators.note: fills means goes into the middle of, so the strike sits inside the other letters

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
to pound or lam is to beat hard

explanation.surface: Ezra Pound fills a poem with something fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' seems to be the poet or money, but it is the verb, meaning hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in the current fashion, so it is a stylish synonym for being trendy.

clue.text: Give hot novel literary dimensions?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A request to make a novel hotter and give it literary depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, which suits 'literary', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a book size, the same as octavo, where a sheet is folded into eight leaves; a page format is a literary dimension.

clue.text: Character giving asset freeze order

definitions.meaning: a character here is a letter written in upper case
an instruction to ..., meaning prevent money being moved

explanation.surface: A financial figure whose order freezes assets.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper-case letter is one kind of written character, and blocking capital is freezing assets.

clue.text: Route with drop in fare

indicators.note: in places the dip inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a route, a narrow road
to sag is to drop or droop

explanation.surface: A route accompanied by a cut in the price of a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like a travel price beside 'Route', but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked Italian pasta dish is an example of fare, meaning food served at a meal.

clue.text: Priest's backing mostly willing union

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the priest is read in reverse

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: game means willing, as in game for anything

explanation.surface: A priest mostly supporting a willing marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LAMA into AMAL; 'mostly' drops the last letter of GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture or blend of things is a union of them, as in a merger of two companies.

clue.text: Did fashion magazine covers cut rather wet French title?

indicators.note: covers means surrounds, so the first pieces sit either side of the damp word

parts.note: to fashion something is to make it, so did fashion means made
Elle is a fashion magazine

indicators.note: cut means the end is chopped off

parts.note: rather wet means damp, or moist

explanation.surface: A fashion magazine asks whether its cover girl was wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' means surrounds, and 'cut' removes the last letter of the damp word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French form of address for an unmarried woman is a title, like Miss in English.

clue.text: Firm lines with mature artwork

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A firm combines straight lines with a mature work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made by sticking pieces of paper or cloth onto a surface is a kind of artwork.

clue.text: Cried, hut walls being not right

indicators.note: walls means surrounds, so the hut encloses the other piece

parts.note: a shed is a hut
a calculation that is not right is out, wrong

explanation.surface: Someone cried because the hut's walls were not right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out loudly is to yell or bellow, the meaning of cried here.

clue.text: Liqueur stocked by wine merchant going around

indicators.note: going around means read in the other direction
stocked by means held within, so the letters are inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A liqueur is stocked by a travelling wine merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocked by' finds the letters in WINE MERCHANT and 'going around' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème is a sweet liqueur, as in crème de menthe.

clue.text: Translating Low German is an enticement to those in school

definitions.text: an enticement to those in school

indicators.note: translating changes words into another form, here a new order of letters

explanation.surface: Translating Low German is an attraction for pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' seems to be pupils, but it is a school of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthworm used as bait is an enticement to a school of fish.

clue.text: Daughter caught in a mist rising over the River Don

indicators.note: in a down answer over means placed above
caught in means trapped inside, so the daughter goes into the reversed mist
in a down answer, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: fog is a thick mist

explanation.surface: A daughter lost in a mist rising above the River Don.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Don' looks like one name; 'River' is R and 'Don' is the definition. 'rising' reverses A FOG to GOFA and 'caught in' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mafia boss is called a don, and the head of a crime family is also known by this title.

clue.text: Fed uncovered report of larceny in gallery?

definitions.meaning: ate outdoors, in the open air
a news line that a picture had been stolen from a gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery's report of a theft after it was uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a meal outdoors in the open air is feeding without a roof overhead, and a stolen picture is a pic nicked.

clue.text: Call for spirit and stiff port, guzzling head of beer

parts.note: to stiff someone is to con or cheat them

indicators.note: head of means the first letter

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A demand for spirits and a stiff port, swallowing some beer too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' and 'port' look like drinks; spirit means verve in music and port is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction means play with vigour, so it is a performer's call for spirit.

clue.text: Pub drink? It's said one shouldn't be trading

indicators.note: it's said tells us to listen to how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: an inn is a pub and cider a drink

explanation.surface: A pub drinker is told they shouldn't be trading.
explanation.walkthrough: Trading on private company knowledge is illegal for those with such access.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with confidential company knowledge is barred from trading shares on it.

clue.text: Leaders of light industry claim high interest in Chinese growth

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Light industry heads claim strong interest in Chinese economic growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese growth' sounds like the economy; it is a fruit growing in China.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee is a fruit tree native to southern China, so a Chinese growth.

clue.text: Dangerous creature from Transylvania's ready to follow traditions

indicators.note: to follow means coming after, so the money comes after the traditions

parts.note: lore is a body of traditions
ready is cash, and Transylvania is in Romania, whose currency is the leu, plural lei

explanation.surface: A dangerous creature from Transylvania, ready to follow tradition: a vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' as cash is British slang (readies).
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend a siren on a Rhine rock lured boatmen to their deaths, so she was a perilous being.

clue.text: Rotter meets end in dock

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a rotter
the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A villain meets his end in the dock of a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a courtroom or a harbour; it is the verb meaning cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock something, like pay or a tail, is to cut it short or reduce it.

clue.text: State in USA — it wants amendment

indicators.note: something that wants amendment needs changing, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A state in the USA needs a constitutional amendment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in USA' looks like it places the state, but those letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African country is a state in the sense of a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Tips for swim past rocky bay in gulf

indicators.note: past means coming after, so the tips follow
rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken up
tips are the ends, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Advice for swimming past a rocky bay into a gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for an abyss, a deep chasm or gulf.

clue.text: Light displays Jaguar door, faded, regularly scratched

indicators.note: regularly scratched means every other letter is struck out, leaving alternate ones

explanation.surface: A Jaguar car's faded door has been scratched.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern and southern lights are natural light displays in the night sky.

clue.text: In sensational fashion, seduce briefly and casually

indicators.note: briefly means shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to lure is to tempt or seduce
idly means casually, without effort

explanation.surface: A casual, brief seduction in a sensational manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking or sensational, so the adverb describes a sensational manner.

clue.text: What traveller may have worn during passage

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the worn piece goes inside the passage

parts.note: a hall is a passage or corridor
old means worn

explanation.surface: What a traveller may have worn while in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' seems to be about clothes the traveller wore; it means old.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bag for carrying clothes and belongings is a typical piece of travel luggage.

clue.text: Try and try to get in satirical poet's good books?

parts.note: to woo someone is to try to get in their favour
Martial was a Roman satirical poet, and getting into his good books is what the wooing aims at

explanation.surface: Trying to win favour with a satirical poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' appears twice: the first is the verb meaning to put on trial; Martial was a Roman writer of epigrams.
explanation.definitionFit: A military tribunal is how the armed forces put a soldier on trial.
